visual_lifecycle.clock: IL-2 simulation time only; pause freezes visual age and never triggers Java-side actor recreation
visual_lifecycle.actor_ownership: The initial head and torus emit for 60 seconds; the ground column remains active through the rise. Ten fixed head layers and five fixed torus layers overlap without moving an active emitter. At 600 seconds the stabilized actor begins; all rise actors are released at 728 seconds after the final 128-second drain. The stabilized emitter stops before 3600 seconds, its particles drain by 3718 seconds, and the 3728-second guard destroys every remaining actor and reference.
visual_lifecycle.note: The historical duration is represented by bounded simulation-time phases inside the 4.09m limits; this is a macroscopic IL-2 adaptation, not CFD.

persistent_visual_state.problem_confirmed: IL-2 4.09m returns a simulation-timed emitter to a small initial state after leaving the pause menu, then visibly replays its age for about five seconds.
persistent_visual_state.diagnostics: Each phase writes event id, simulation age, surface, actor counts, heartbeat, drain state and emission state to the game log.
persistent_visual_state.replacement: The failed pause watcher, real-time clock and actor rehydration are removed. The same simulation-timed actors remain owned across pause; recreating an IL-2 emitter is forbidden because it restarts the particle age.
persistent_visual_state.rise_curve: Fixed layers follow a quadratic ease-out from the historical airburst to the AGL summit over 600 simulated seconds. The target is computed from local terrain altitude. No live emitter is moved because IL-2 leaves previously emitted particles in world space.
persistent_visual_state.runtime_verdict: Run 20260903-160537Z rejected the moving-emitter candidate: the moving origin rose while the existing particle mass remained low. Both detonations stayed responsive and stable. The fixed-layer replacement passes all offline checks but remains untested in game.

cloud_summit.interpretation: approximate height above local ground including the historical airburst altitude

fixed_layer_altitudes_agl_m.note: The first ten values are fixed rise-layer origins; the final value is the stabilized origin. Particle bounds extend beyond these anchors.

intentional_engine_adaptations: The stock IL-2 inverse-square TNT falloff is restored instead of granting full nuclear power everywhere inside the radius.
The 2 psi historical planning radius becomes the bounded engine-damage radius after airburst geometry and cube-root yield scaling.
The 1 psi and 0.5 psi outer knots and the aircraft velocity coupling are documented gameplay approximations, not historical source values.
Wave delay samples actor distance at detonation; impulse direction uses the actor position at arrival, but moving-target interception is not continuously recomputed.
Thermal flash is visual in this iteration; thermal burns and ionizing radiation are not simulated.
No crater is spawned for the historical airbursts.
The legacy bomb50_land nuclear follow-up is removed only from the nuclear branch.
The primary cloud reaches the stabilized phase after ten simulated minutes and completes after one simulated hour; pausing must consume neither interval.
Pause and camera culling never cause Java-side actor recreation; flash, fireball and shock are never replayed by the lifecycle controller.
Phase changes overlap for one maximum particle lifetime, avoiding abrupt cuts while remaining bounded by the 3 728-second cleanup deadline.
